title: bn254-pairing-inversion: GT rho with a constant-time step and a 31,302-instruction static price, plus [x]P0, time_log2 = 130.091157

claims.statement: For the protected BN254 profile, the single-trial algorithm of proof.md recovers x with g^x=z and outputs (P=[x]P0, Q=Q0) with e(P,Q)=z, with success probability at least 0.85 over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins, and every run performs at most W < 2^130.091157 units (log2 W = 130.091156869), one unit being C=20,000 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents. The bilinear reduction and collision recovery are as in the earlier package; the GT walk step is now constant-time (no conditional branch, no loop, no early return in its compiled call graph), so one step costs exactly 31,302 instructions on every input, a static count from the shipped disassembly (STATIC_BOUND.txt; Callgrind confirms 31,302 Ir per step on 10 production tables with a different salt every step). Scalars come from a capped SHA-256 counter-mode sampler (K=64 attempts per scalar, strict v<r, abort counted as failure, union bound 2^-13.30). Uniformity, independence, the 1/r degeneracy and the abort bound are exact in the ideal independent-word model and heuristic with additive distinguishing advantage eps under the PRF assumption. The 0.85 success figure is a random-map heuristic supported by small-subgroup evidence at order 43,913, not a production measurement. The G1 part is deterministic and charged at a fixed 2^24.

experiments.purpose: Recompute every ledger row from r and the static 31,302-instruction step price; check the declared rational is the rounded-up log2(W); recompute the capped sampler failure bound and measure acceptance; verify the mixer transliteration against the binary's hashdump; run the 32-adding walk in the order-43,913 subgroup of the real BN254 Fp12; and regenerate/compare the G1 vectors from y^2=x^3+3, P0=(1,2). The constant-time step is checked separately by static_count.py.
